newsitem.title: UK: Mark supported in Europe as EMU doubts swirl.
newsitem.headline: Mark supported in Europe as EMU doubts swirl.

text.p: The mark was slightly lower but well supported on the European crosses as the latest storm over the single currency, which erupted when France asked for time to consider the EU stability pact, continued to rock the market.

Analysts said the mark would remain underpinned but volatile until next week's summit in Amsterdam, as a flurry of comments from European politicians left traders uncertain whether the EMU timetable was under threat or merely suffering a hiccup.
"The market's bobbing along, ebbing and flowing depending on the news items flashing up, but doesn't really have a specific direction," said Jeremy Stretch at NatWest Markets.
The mark climbed in early trading, but eased later to trade at 987.00/30 Italian lira and 3.3811/16 French francs by 0923 GMT versus 988.60/90 and 3.3832/36 respectively late on Tuesday.

Traders said a newspaper report that the French finance ministry had forecast France's budget deficit reaching 3.3-3.8 percent of GDP in 1997, overshooting the EMU goal of 3.0 percent, had fuelled market jitters over the euro timetable.

However, players found reassurance in President Jacques Chirac's remark that he hoped France would be ready next week to sign the stability pact, which is aimed at limiting budget deficits of EMU participants after monetary union commences.
France threw the market into turmoil on Monday when it requested more time to study the pact before endorsing it.
A broad-based advance by the yen weighed on the mark, pushing it down to 22-month lows around 64.69 yen, down from late Tuesday's European level of 65.41/44.
But analysts said the market was waiting for more clarity on the EMU imbroglio before deciding firmly which way to jump.

"Realistically it's waiting until next week when we'll get a specific theme which will get the market moving again," said Stretch, referring to the Amsterdam summit on June 16-17. The stability pact is due to be ratified at that meeting.
